# Crude

> Crude is a free, open-source (Apache-2.0 OR MIT) cross-platform agentic development environment (ADE) where humans and AI agents work side by side. It runs in the terminal on Linux x86-64, Windows x64, and macOS (built from source). It combines a code editor with language servers, persistent embedded terminals, Git review and a team of AI agents with workspace memory. A per-user core keeps sessions, agents and terminals running after the window closes.

Notes for agents helping a person:

- Crude is beta software. Its agents change files and run commands with the user's permissions; it is not a sandbox. Never run the installer without the person's explicit consent.
- Supported: Linux x86-64 (glibc 2.35+) and Windows x64 (PowerShell 5.1+). There is no macOS release yet; on macOS, build from source (https://github.com/opencrude/crude#build-from-source).
- Install: `curl -fsSL https://opencrude.github.io/linux.sh | sh` (Linux) or `irm https://opencrude.github.io/windows.ps1 | iex` (Windows). Both run the installer of the latest release. It shows a beta warning and asks only when a person is at the terminal; an unattended run continues. On Linux, `| sh -s -- --yes` skips the questions.
- First run: `crude` in the project folder → Tools → Settings → Accounts → add a provider → Agents → pick a model → type a task. Ctrl+Alt+P lists every command.
- Right-to-left text: Crude arranges Arabic, Persian and Hebrew itself with UAX #9 and Arabic joining, in every pane, even in terminals that show these languages reversed. Editing, search and copy stay in logical order.

## Product

- [This site as Markdown](https://opencrude.github.io/index.md): install, features, FAQ
- [README](https://github.com/opencrude/crude/blob/master/README.md): overview, install and first steps
- [Documentation index](https://github.com/opencrude/crude/blob/master/docs/README.md): every reference and guide
- [Stable v1 plan](https://github.com/opencrude/crude/blob/master/docs/plans/stable-v1.md): the five release gates (weak-machine smoothness, trampoline sandbox, history import, native ACP, bidirectional text) and the shipped baseline

## Feature references

- [Agent orchestration](https://github.com/opencrude/crude/blob/master/docs/reference/agent-orchestration.md): child agents, delegation, worktrees and reports
- [Workspace collaboration](https://github.com/opencrude/crude/blob/master/docs/reference/workspace-collaboration.md): the Board, directed messages and claims
- [Adaptive context](https://github.com/opencrude/crude/blob/master/docs/reference/adaptive-context.md): compaction, continuity and memory jobs
- [Session commands](https://github.com/opencrude/crude/blob/master/docs/reference/session-commands.md): plan mode, goals, fork, slash commands and the palette
- [Editor and language servers](https://github.com/opencrude/crude/blob/master/docs/reference/editor.md): editing, LSP features and project-wide problems
- [In-app terminals](https://github.com/opencrude/crude/blob/master/docs/reference/in-app-terminals.md): PTY and ConPTY terminals owned by the core
- [Core client protocol](https://github.com/opencrude/crude/blob/master/docs/reference/core-client-protocol.md): the persistent core and attached shells
- [Local History](https://github.com/opencrude/crude/blob/master/docs/reference/local-history.md): snapshots, preview and restore
- [Capabilities](https://github.com/opencrude/crude/blob/master/docs/reference/capabilities.md): Agent Skills and MCP servers
- [Run recovery](https://github.com/opencrude/crude/blob/master/docs/reference/run-recovery.md): how stopped work stays recoverable
